topic: Instantaneous Rate of Change and the Derivative

sections.title: The Problem of Average Speed
sections.content: Begin with the prerequisite of average speed (change in distance / change in time). Visualize a cheetah running along a straight path. Calculate the average speed over a 5-second interval.
sections.example: A cheetah runs 100 meters in 5 seconds. Average speed = 100/5 = 20 m/s. But did it run exactly 20 m/s the whole time?

sections.title: Shrinking the Interval (The Secant Line)
sections.content: Introduce the visual of a secant line connecting two points on a distance-time graph. Show what happens to the slope of this line as the time interval Δt gets smaller and smaller.
sections.example: Zooming in on the graph: Shrink the time interval from 5s to 1s, then 0.1s. The secant line gradually overlaps with the curve.

sections.title: Defining Instantaneous Rate (The Tangent Line)
sections.content: Define the derivative as the limit of the average rate of change as Δt approaches zero. Explain that the secant line transforms into a tangent line at a specific point.
sections.example: Animation: As Δt → 0, the two points on the cheetah's path merge into one. The slope of the tangent line represents the cheetah's 'speedometer' reading at that exact moment.

sections.title: Formalizing the Derivative
sections.content: Present the mathematical definition: f'(x) = lim(h→0) [f(x+h) - f(x)] / h. Connect the visual slope (m) to the symbolic notation.
sections.example: Equation display: f'(x) represents the 'instantaneous' change, providing the exact velocity of the cheetah at any time 't'.

sections.title: Application and Summary
sections.content: Summarize that the derivative is the slope of the tangent line and represents the instantaneous rate of change. Challenge students to think of other rates.
sections.example: Beyond physics: How fast is a balloon inflating (rate of volume change) or how fast is a bank account growing (rate of interest) at a specific second?
